description: H. W. Lenstra, Jr. and Carl Pomerance, A rigorous time bound for factoring integers, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 5 (1992), no. 3, 483-516, doi 10.1090/S0894-0347-1992-1137100-0. Abstract: a probabilistic algorithm is presented that finds the prime factorization of any positive integer n in expected time L_n[1/2, 1+o(1)], where L_n[a, c] = exp(c (log n)^a (log log n)^(1-a)). The algorithm never gives a wrong answer (it is Las Vegas: random class groups of imaginary quadratic fields). No assumption: the bound is unconditional. Time e^{(1+o(1)) sqrt(ln N ln ln N)} = 2^{(log N)^{1/2+o(1)}}: theta = 1/2. It is the rigorous record that the 2026 agent claims cite (Ops brief, 2026-11-27); Dixon (1981) had L_N[1/2, 2 sqrt 2]. The heuristic number field sieve, L_N[1/3, (64/9)^(1/3)], is not proved and is not a baseline.
